title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to a computation, from 1978 onward (Esquisse period), of automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere P^1 \ {0,1,∞} that commute with the symmetries S_J, |J| = 3, and with complex conjugation τ. The previous page (6) derived equations (12) on a pair (ρ, β): ρ ∈ Ẑ^* is a 'multiplicateur' with γ = (ρ-1)/2, and β ∈ π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 - 3 points), free profinite on two generators. The equations are β·σ_∞(β) = 1 and α ρ^{-1}(α) ρ^{-2}(α) = 1 with α = l_1^γ β. Here σ_∞ is the involution exchanging the punctures 0 and 1, and ρ in the exponent is the order-3 rotation. These are exactly Drinfeld's two defining relations of \hat{GT}: (I) f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and (II) f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1 with m = (λ-1)/2.

The figure is the sphere with three holes a_0, a_1, a_∞ centred on the real equator. R_i^± are base points just to either side of each hole. a_i^± are the two half-loops around hole i joining R_i^+ and R_i^-. The arcs c run along the equator. Π_J is the groupoid with these base points; the earlier b_i^ω are equator arcs joining R-points of consecutive holes. ω ∈ {+,-} is a cyclic orientation of J, ωi is the successor of i, and ω' is the opposite orientation.

On this page Grothendieck adds new base points Q_i (i ∈ J), one on each of the three real intervals. He adds arcs c_i^ω : Q_i → R^{ω'}_{ω'i}, permuted simply transitively by S_J. Then:
- (13) b_i^ω = c_i^ω (c_i^{ω'})^{-1}, so the b's are no longer needed as generators and relation (12)(a), the 2-cycle relation, becomes automatic.
- (14) To write part (b), the 3-cycle relation, he defines ã_i^ω = (c_{ωi}^ω)^{-1} a_i^ω c_{ω'i}^{ω'} : Q_{ω'i} → Q_{ωi}. This is the half-loop around puncture i, transported to the midpoints of the two adjacent real intervals. The first, crossed-out formula was wrong.
- (15) The ã are permuted simply transitively by S_J, and τ(ã_i^ω) = (ã_i^{ω'})^{-1}.
- (16) Relation (b) becomes the 'triangle' relation ã_{ωi}^ω ã_{ω'i}^ω ã_i^ω = 1. Going half-way around each of the three punctures in turn closes up. There are two essentially distinct relations, one per orientation, swapped by τ.
- (17) He rigidifies the vertex groups π(Q_i) = π_1(Σ_J(C), Q_i) by isomorphisms ψ_i^ω : π_{0,3} → π(Q_i). Each is the composite of φ^{ω'}_{ω'i} : π_{0,3} → π(R^{ω'}_{ω'i}) with transport by (c_i^ω)^{-1}. NB: τψ_i^ω(g) = ψ_i^{ω'}(conjugate/twisted g).
- (18) The two rigidifications at Q_i differ by the involution σ_∞.
- (19) Transport along ã_i^ω acts on these coordinates by ε_0, the order-3 automorphism of π_{0,3} induced by the cyclic permutation of the punctures, or by σ_∞ε_0, ε_0σ_∞, etc. Overbraces name these composites by ρ^{±1}.

Purpose: re-present the groupoid with S_3-symmetric real base points, so that an automorphism u is coded by data at the Q's. On the next page this is u(c_i^ω) = c_i^ω ψ_i^ω(η). Then β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}, which solves the 2-cycle equation identically, and only the 3-cycle equation (24) in α = l_0^γ σ_∞(η)η^{-1} remains. Here l_0^γ is the inertia-type twist on the half-loops from page 6 (u(a_i^ω) = a_i^ω φ(l_0^γ)). In modern terms this is the passage from tangential base points to real 'mid-interval' base points in Drinfeld/Ihara's description of \hat{GT} acting on \hat{F}_2.
errors: The first version of (14), (a_{ω i}^{ω'})^{-1} a_i^{ω'} c..., is crossed out and replaced by the correct composite (c_{ωi}^ω)^{-1} a_i^ω c_{ω'i}^{ω'}. The scribbled-out figure next to it reflects that correction.

Notation clash: ρ denotes both the multiplier ρ ∈ Ẑ^* (with γ = (ρ-1)/2) and, in the overbraces of (19) and in (12), the order-3 automorphism ε_0σ_∞ (or its inverse) of π_{0,3}. This makes formulas like α ρ^{-1}(α) ρ^{-2}(α) = 1 ambiguous on first reading.
The NB after (17), τψ_i^ω(g) = ψ_i^{ω'}(...), is not fully legible. Its argument (conjugated or twisted g) cannot be confirmed, and its consistency with (18) is not checked on the page.

(13) presupposes that the arcs c_i^ω and c_i^{ω'} land at the R-points bounding b_i^ω with compatible indexing (ω'i vs ωi). The indexing is not spelled out and is easy to get wrong. No mathematical error is evident beyond the corrected (14).

ideas.what: Adding S_3-symmetric real base points Q_i on the three real intervals of P^1(R) \ {0,1,∞}, connected by real arcs to base points near the punctures, so that the 2-cycle relation becomes automatic and only the 3-cycle relation remains.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with tangential/real base points; 'Lego' or Teichmüller groupoid presentation of π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for the Lego/base-point philosophy; Deligne 1989 and Ihara for tangential base points; Drinfeld 1990 for GT
ideas.where_published: Spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (§2, the 'Lego' of the Teichmüller tower) and likely La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); these exact formulas: unsure

ideas.what: Half-loops ã_i^ω between midpoints of adjacent real intervals, with τ(ã^ω) = (ã^{ω'})^{-1} and the triangle relation ã ã ã = 1 (two orientations swapped by complex conjugation).
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation for the profinite free group; the 'triangle' presentation of π_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere

ideas.what: Rigidifications ψ_i^ω : π_{0,3} → π(Q_i), with transition automorphisms σ_∞ (order 2) and ε_0 (order 3) generating the S_3-action on π̂_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: S_3 = Aut(P^1, {0,1,∞}) acting on \hat F_2 by outer automorphisms; standard coordinates x, y, z with xyz = 1

ideas.what: Context from pages 6 and 8: the (ρ, β) equations are exactly Drinfeld's \hat{GT} relations (I) and (II) with γ = (ρ-1)/2. The 2-cycle relation is solved by β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}, coding u by its value η on the arcs to the real base points.
ideas.modern_name: Defining equations of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group \hat{GT}; coboundary parametrization of solutions of f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1
ideas.where_published: Esquisse describes the programme but does not write the equations

missed.claim: Together with pages 6 and 8, this page shows Grothendieck deriving the defining relations of \hat{GT} from a groupoid presentation, apparently before Drinfeld (1990). This uses an S_3-symmetric set of real base points, with the two 3-cycle relations interchanged by complex conjugation and the multiplier exponent γ = (ρ-1)/2 in place. This page performs the base-point change that reduces the system to a single 3-cycle equation.
missed.quote: (16) ã_{ωi}^ω ã_{ω'i}^ω ã_i^ω = 1 (deux relations essent. distinctes, qui sont permutées par τ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It strengthens the historical attribution of the explicit \hat{GT} equations to unpublished Grothendieck work. It also shows a presentation where the equations are organised by the S_3 × ⟨τ⟩ symmetry of P^1(R) minus three points.

missed.claim: Coding an automorphism by its effect η on paths from punctures to real mid-interval base points makes the 2-cycle relation automatic (β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}). This is a 'half-f' parametrization. It is legitimate profinitely: H^1(Z/2, \hat F_2) for the swap involution is trivial, since involutions of Ẑ ⋆ Z/2 are conjugate to the factor. The parametrization resembles later tricks (Nakamura-Schneps, Furusho) but Grothendieck's version is S_3/τ-equivariant from the start.
missed.quote: permutés de façon simplement transitive par 𝔖_J ... (13) b_i^ω = c_i^ω (c_i^{ω'})^{-1} (donc les b_i^ω deviennent inutiles...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Reducing \hat{GT} to a single 3-cycle equation in α after a coboundary substitution is relevant to recent work showing that relation (I) or parts of the defining relations are redundant (e.g. Furusho's results on associators). It may be worth comparing.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a technical change of base points, but it sits inside a pre-Drinfeld derivation of the exact \hat{GT} equations (multiplier γ = (ρ-1)/2, 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations) with a symmetric real-base-point formalism. It is notable as unpublished detail. Specialists (e.g. Schneps) are partly aware that Grothendieck computed such things, so this is not a radical surprise.
transcription_corrections: The heading 'II_J' at left is very likely 'Π_J', the name of the groupoid (cf. 'Π̂_3' on the next page).

In (14), the crossed-out first expression reads approximately (a_{ω'i}^{ω})^{-1} a_i^{ω} c_{ω'i}^{ω'}. The corrected expression, written below, is (c_{ωi}^{ω})^{-1} a_i^{ω} c_{ω'i}^{ω'} : Q_{ω'i} → Q_{ωi}.
First line of (19): the left side and the subscripts use starred ω* (ã_i^{ω*}, ψ_{ω*i}^{ω*}), not plain ω. The overbrace on σ_∞ε_0 reads something like 'τ_∞(ρ)'.
Second line of (19): the overbrace on (ε_0σ_∞) is labelled 'ρ^{-1}', and the last term is ψ(σ_∞ε_0σ_∞(g)).
The NB after (17) is only partly legible: τψ_i^ω(g) = ψ_i^{ω'}( ... g) with some twist (τ_0 or ε_0) on the argument rather than a plain bar.
'Pour repérer les π(Q_i) = π_1(Σ_J(ℂ), Q_i)': the 'π(Q_i) =' is an interlinear insertion above π_1.
